segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: The analytics dashboard needs one change before the next release. Customer revenue information shouldn't be visible to everyone.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Is this about all analytics or specifically the revenue-related metrics?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Specifically revenue, average order value, and the monthly customer value figures.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: We are expanding into two new markets next month, and our customer numbers are expected to increase significantly. Some of our internal sales information is sensitive because we're negotiating with another company right now. I don't want ordinary support staff seeing the revenue numbers.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Understood. So support staff shouldn't see those metrics, but administrators should?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yes. Admins and finance managers can see them. Regular support users shouldn't.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: We already have the RBAC system with ADMIN and FINANCE roles. We could enforce the restriction at the API level rather than changing authentication.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That sounds reasonable. Does the frontend also need to hide the cards?

segments.speaker: Neha
segments.text: Yes. If the API denies access but the cards remain visible, users will just see errors.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Then let's do both. Ravi, handle the API authorization. Neha, hide the revenue cards for unauthorized users.

segments.speaker: Ravi
segments.text: I'll take the backend part. I'll check the existing RBAC middleware and update the relevant analytics endpoints.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Neha, can you also add the unauthorized-state handling?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Ravi, have this ready by Friday. Neha, same deadline.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: QA should verify that admins and finance managers can see the metrics and support users cannot.
